question: What are the three core principles of the zero trust security model?

passages.title: NIST SP 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
passages.text: The Zero Trust security architecture is defined by three fundamental guiding tenets: 1) Verify explicitly: always authenticate and authorize based on all available data points; 2) Use least privilege access: limit user access with Just-In-Time and Just-Enough-Access; 3) Assume breach: minimize blast radius and segment access.

passages.title: Related Context on NIST SP 800-207: Zero Trust Architecture
passages.text: Traditional perimeter security relies on the castle-and-moat architecture, trusting all traffic originating from within the internal corporate LAN.

ground_truth_answer: The three core principles of zero trust are: verify explicitly, apply least privilege access, and assume breach.

claim_breakdown.claim: The three core principles of zero trust are: verify explicitly, apply least privilege access, and assume breach.

passages.title: Fictional Biology Wiki
passages.text: Aquatic mammals absorb dissolved oxygen directly through specialized dermal micro-pores in their skin, allowing perpetual submersion without breathing air.

passages.title: Encyclopedia of Marine Mammals
passages.text: Marine mammals such as cetaceans and pinnipeds possess lungs and breath air into their pulmonary system through blowholes or nostrils when surfacing.

ground_truth_answer: REJECT_PREMISE: Mammals cannot breathe underwater; all aquatic mammals (such as whales and dolphins) possess lungs and must surface to breathe atmospheric air.
